assumptions: The flag flip is inferred from the service's own per-minute flag-evaluation log lines. The flag provider's change history was queried three times and reported zero recent changes, so the change was never corroborated at its source; either the provider's history is incomplete or the flag state changed by some path that does not record history.
No deployment was found in lookback windows ranging from 24 hours to roughly 8 days, so a code change is assumed not to be involved. This rests on the change-event feed being complete.

The link between the flag and the ZeroDivisionError is inferred from timing and the flag's name plus the log text; no stack trace, code diff, or source inspection was performed to confirm which expression divides by zero or why the divisor is zero.

The pre-existing UpstreamTimeout errors on account pages (visible from 23:37 onward, including 00:03-00:05) are assumed to be unrelated background noise rather than a contributor to the burst, on the grounds that they are a different error class and predate the flip.

The incident's recorded end time reflects escalation to a human, not verified recovery. The last log line read (00:13) still shows the flag on and account-page errors continuing, and no mitigating action was taken, so the resolution and its timing are not attributable to anything the automation did.
Impact is assumed to be confined to account page rendering; no other endpoints or services were examined.
input.executive_summary: Shortly after midnight UTC on 14 September, a new billing-related feature was switched on for the online shop. The newly activated code crashed whenever it tried to render a customer's account page, so customers who opened their account page during the event got an error instead. Errors began at 00:07 UTC, monitoring alerted at 00:12, and the automated responder worked the incident until 00:14, when it handed off to a human; errors were still occurring in the last logs it read. Automation diagnosed the cause with high confidence within about thirty seconds, but it had no safe, reversible action available to it — the feature-flag system reported no recent changes it could undo — so it declined to act, retried the same investigation three times, and escalated. Nothing was changed in production by the automation, and no confirmed recovery was observed before hand-off; the human responder should turn the feature off and confirm account pages render again. The follow-up work is to make the flag reversible from the responder's tooling and to fix the division-by-zero in the monthly-spend calculation before re-enabling the feature.
input.root_cause: The `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop went from off to on at 00:07 UTC (mixed 97 off / 103 on during that minute, fully on from 00:08), enabling a code path that divides by zero while computing monthly spend during account page rendering; every request that hit the new path failed with ZeroDivisionError. A pre-existing, low-level trickle of UpstreamTimeout errors on the same page was present before the flip and is a separate background condition, not the cause of the burst.
